claims.text: The meter goes live: it charges by how far down a page you scroll, lets the balance go below zero forever, shows one small balance in the top bar, and lets you refuse to pay with a reason.
claims.quote: It charges by how far down a page you scroll, it lets your balance go below zero forever

claims.text: Paying is one £5 payment on Stripe, with no account, no subscription and nothing that renews.
claims.quote: Paying is one £5 payment on Stripe.

claims.text: The price is a hypothesis: 10p for a new article read to the end, 5p for an older one, less for other pages, and it could be wrong either way.
claims.quote: 10p for a new article read to the end, 5p for an older one, less for other pages.

value.unit: pence for a new article read to the end

claims.text: The bet is that people pay for reading when nothing forces them to, if what they get back is a site that knows what they read, with the history kept on their own machine.
claims.quote: people pay for reading when nothing forces them to, if what they get back is a site that knows what they read

claims.text: A page's price is what it costs read to the end, times the share you scrolled through, never less than a tenth.
claims.quote: You pay that times the share you scrolled through, never less than a tenth.

claims.text: At the foot of an article, four reasons not to be charged; the charge is refunded and the reason kept in the reader's history as a signal that shapes their picks.
claims.quote: The charge is refunded, and the reason is kept in your history as a signal.

claims.text: The meter is rebuilt as SG Meter, a web component another site can add with a script tag and a config.
claims.quote: so another site can add it with a script tag and a config

claims.text: The Guardian counts what you read in the browser's own storage, a weekly count per tag starting on a Monday, and uses the count to ask for support.
claims.quote: The count is used to ask you for support.

claims.text: Press Gazette reported in September 2025 that the Guardian's digital reader revenue rose 22%, from £88m to £107m in the year to the end of March 2025.
claims.quote: from £88m in 2023/2024 to £107m in the year to the end of March 2025

claims.text: The Guardian's middle tier sells, in part, the absence of the ask, and every tier is a subscription decided in advance for reading that has not happened.
claims.quote: The middle tier sells, in part, the absence of the ask. And every tier is a subscription

claims.text: A reader who can see an honest running total and is never shamed for it is more willing to settle it than one who is counted and asked.
claims.quote: a reader who can see an honest running total, and who is never shamed for it, is more willing to settle it than one who is counted and asked

claims.text: Added the same day in v0.7.34, the reader sets part of the price: three scales at the foot, where usefulness of 1 is free, 3 the price and 5 double.
claims.quote: A page is now charged only as much as you read it and only as much as you say it was worth.

claims.text: Depth is measured on the main column, rounded to 5%, at most once every 400 milliseconds; it is not reading time and not attention.
claims.quote: It is not reading time and it is not attention; a reader can scroll to the bottom without reading.

claims.text: A charge tells the site nothing; a refusal with a reason is the first thing a reader has told it about a page without being asked to write anything.
claims.quote: A charge tells us nothing; everyone who scrolled was charged.

claims.text: Declines are kept in the reader's browser and used there to push topics down their picks; the site does not see them unless the reader sends their history.
claims.quote: They are kept in the reader's history, in their browser, like everything else, and used there

claims.text: Prices were raised from the first version's 5p and 3p on purpose, because a price too low teaches nothing.
claims.quote: a price that is too low teaches nothing, because nobody would ever notice paying it

claims.text: Stripe's listed UK fee for a standard card is 1.5% plus 20p, so on £5 it is 27.5p and £4.72 reaches the site, about 94.5%.
claims.quote: On £5 that is 27.5p, so £4.72 reaches the site, about 94.5%.

value.unit: GBP reaching the site per top-up

claims.text: The fixed 20p is why the top-up is £5 and not £1, where a standard card would take more than a fifth.
claims.quote: The fixed 20p is why the top-up is £5 and not £1

claims.text: None of the revenue rows pays for anything that matters; the case is evidence, a shape to test personalisation against, and a library.
claims.quote: None of those rows pays for anything that matters. That is not the case for doing this.

claims.text: Paul Feldman's unwatched bagel boxes were paid for about 87% of the time by 2001, against the 90% he would call honest.
claims.quote: about 87% of bagels were paid for by 2001

claims.text: For Radiohead's In Rainbows, comScore estimated 38% of downloaders paid something, 48% in the UK, averaging about $6 among payers and $2.26 across everyone.
claims.quote: 38% of downloaders paid something (48% in the UK)

claims.text: In Gneezy's theme park experiment 0.5% bought at $12.95, 8.39% bought when paying what they wanted at 92 cents on average, and 4.49% at $5.33 when half went to charity.
claims.quote: When riders could pay what they wanted, 8.39% bought, paying 92 cents on average.

value.unit: % who bought when paying what they wanted

claims.text: Remove the force and many more people take part while the average payment falls; a small stated price per page sits between the two.
claims.quote: Remove the force and many more people take part, while the average payment falls.

claims.text: The review is eight weeks after the Stripe link goes live; the link went live on newsroom.sgit.ai on 11 October 2026, so the review is on 6 December 2026.
claims.quote: the link went live on newsroom.sgit.ai today, so the review is on 6 December 2026

claims.text: H1: someone pays when nothing forces them to, with a first real payment within 14 days; no payment in 14 days proves it wrong.
claims.quote: A first real payment within 14 days

claims.text: H2: at least 10 different payers by the review; fewer than 5 proves it wrong.
claims.quote: At least 10 different payers by the review

claims.text: H3: paying is a habit, with at least 3 payers paying a second time; no repeat payment proves it wrong.
claims.quote: At least 3 payers pay a second time

claims.text: H4: making cheating easy costs nothing that reaches the site, with no disputes or chargebacks.
claims.quote: Making cheating easy costs nothing that reaches us

claims.text: H5, that below zero is normal, cannot be tested without readers sending their history; it is written down so the team notices if it starts believing it without evidence.
claims.quote: We cannot test this without readers sending their history

claims.text: What can be seen is the Stripe dashboard and LinkedIn's views; what cannot is anything the meter records, because there is no analytics and the meter sends nothing.
claims.quote: There is no analytics on this site, and the meter sends nothing.

claims.text: If nobody pays, the first suspect is not the price but that the trade is invisible; the picks get better before the meter gets louder.
claims.quote: We would make the picks better before we made the meter louder.

claims.text: Anyone can cheat by editing the balance, opening a private window, or faking a payment reference; each changes a number only the cheater sees and costs a payment never due.
claims.quote: Each of those changes a number only the cheater can see, and costs the site a payment it was never going to receive.

claims.text: Written from a voice note by Dinis Cruz by a Claude Code session on 10 October 2026; the meter is SG Meter v1.0.0 and its prices are the METER rules in the build.
claims.quote: The meter is SG Meter v1.0.0
